label: Day 1, Feb 25
summary: Debugging a body system crash, system architecture principles, website deployment, and task management.
description: R&D daily sprint with Alex Chen, Nina Torres, and Greg Palmer. Topics: body system crash caused by a 6.5M character spam page, discussion on component isolation as an engineering principle, website deployment issues with Vercel, Mycelium project scoping, OS project prototyping plans, analytics feature request for session time tracking, and task management tool selection.

data.chunk: Nina Torres: Hello. Alex Chen: Hello. Greg Palmer: Good morning. Alex Chen: You are in a cafe. I'm going to also go work from cafe today later in afternoon. Cool. What's up? Yesterday I couldn't work at all. I mean I was working but on body — we couldn't figure it out at the end of the day but this morning I figured it out. Greg Palmer: What was it? Was it the new implementation? Alex Chen: So carefinder sends URLs to body to get enhanced. It was crawling everything, but one of these websites out of thousands — one of them has like 25 pages and one of the pages has this hello world page that has 6.5 million characters.

Alex Chen: It's a spam repellent. The crawler was crawling it and trying to digest it and it overwhelmed the whole process. Greg Palmer: Is it the new implementation or the old? Alex Chen: The old — that was the problem, nothing has changed. The only symptom was that viate couldn't clean after itself when it created the shards. Greg Palmer: That's the worst kind of bug. Alex Chen: Yesterday we decided to just rewrite the whole crawling part for stories. This morning when I crawled it in isolation, cloud noticed it and says hey it has 6.5 million characters. Greg Palmer: This is why it's important to have a reproducible local development environment where you can run components in isolation.

Alex Chen: Isolation — yeah, that's the problem. The way Daniel architects things, everything works together as a machine. I'm pretty sure he knows how to isolate them, but it's not his first principle. Greg Palmer: For me I can't write another way — I write something small, test it, write something else, put them together, everything works together but also in isolation. Alex Chen: Exactly. Everything has to work in isolation like a function. Input, output. That's it. Period. That's how I also wrote Nexus. Nina Torres: Is that one of those principles? Greg Palmer: That's actually like every complex, every functional —

Greg Palmer: Every complex system inevitably evolved from a simpler system. And the opposite is also true — complex systems cannot be made to work when you are already starting with that. We should put this in our engineering manifesto. Alex Chen: I think it's like Lego. You can't have one brick that is broken — you need to fix that and then connect it to another one. Nina Torres: That's what I mean. Alex Chen: Oh, there are new type of Legos — they're not from the Lego company, but they are super tiny and it's so obsessive. As soon as you start building with them, you can't stop. Nina Torres: This morning, my trainer called me obsessed because I've been going yesterday and today and I'm going to go tomorrow.

Nina Torres: She was like, "Do you want to also come Friday?" Alex Chen: What do you do? Weightlifting or — Nina Torres: No, it's functional patterns. It's a lot about body posture and doing exercises. It's similar to the Lego idea because you do exercises isolated and then that becomes how you move throughout your day. Alex Chen: I went to physiotherapy a few months back when I had the back problem and he started talking about exercises about fascia. Nina Torres: That's exactly it. For the first month all I did was massaging my fascia with rollers. Greg Palmer: Actually the person we stayed with in Rotterdam — they are this kind of physiotherapist, functional patterns, fascia focused.

Greg Palmer: So if you want, it's literally 10 minutes walk from space. I can hook you up. Alex Chen: Do they have a website? You can send it to me. The exercises are fun — the first thing they were saying is just even if you're washing dishes, move. That was the key principle. Greg Palmer: That's why I have this chair — it's really good because I can move. It actually makes you move. But I also have to, because of ADHD restlessness and stuff.

Alex Chen: So yeah, Vercel failed. I need to still fix the image on deployment for the website. Apart from that I think we are good — I can take care of the website today. Greg Palmer: Maybe some of the blog posts need to be cut out. Basically just a review — see what blog posts we should remove. I think each of us should have a pass also on phone. Check the online version, check the content, flag anything that should be removed. Then I think we're good. Nina Torres: Yeah, I want to add something to the landing page.

Alex Chen: I'm going to also look into other solutions than Vercel. I don't want to make it a bottleneck but it's good if you guys also have access. Greg Palmer: I already set up Cloudflare. It's very easy to deploy. Alex Chen: Let's not make a task for now — let's just have the website launch and then figure it out. Greg Palmer: Yeah. I'm continuing with specifying what to build for Mycelium — more in the technical sense, defining the scope of what would be a good slice. I've made some progress with the planning.

Greg Palmer: I guess we should talk about the inhab project — maybe we can do that separately. Alex Chen: Yeah, let's do that. Nina Torres: So the analytics — Alex has permissions right? Alex Chen: That's something we need to still test with Greg because yesterday I was getting an error. Greg Palmer: Let's do that separately. Alex Chen: Do we want to do our brainstorming on the OS thing today as planned? Greg Palmer: I don't have anything new.

Alex Chen: I have the same feeling that it's a bit too early — we need time to process. Greg, you need to also show what you have in mind. Greg Palmer: I really want to build. Nina Torres: Then take the time to build. Would it help to push this session to Friday? Alex Chen: You know what helps? You could also just make a fake interface with Gemini's AI studio — just to show how you envision it. Because that prototype I made in Gemini shows exactly what I have in mind. Greg Palmer: That's a really good idea. I like that approach.

Alex Chen: So it's more like Photoshop it for now. No code. Greg Palmer: Yeah, that makes sense. Nina Torres: Okay, so then it makes sense maybe Friday. Alex Chen: Friday is better — we can always block Fridays for working together sessions like mini workshops or hackathons. Once you have that Gemini prototype you can share it and everyone could make a different version or add to it. That's what Figma should have had — such a feature, but they don't. Greg Palmer: Okay, I like that. Then yeah, that's it I think.

Greg Palmer: Let's fix your permissions. Nina Torres: And can you then add the time spent in the app? Alex Chen: Yeah, sure. For Cibil I haven't spent much time apart from the meetings. Nina Torres: And what about the contract? Alex Chen: I sent it to Morgan on Monday. I should probably send her another reminder today. Nina Torres: So you will update the time spent in the app. Greg Palmer: That's a new analytics. Nina Torres: It's the new analytics that Morgan was asking. Alex Chen: Do we have a card for it or somewhere that is defined?

Nina Torres: I've been asking about it for a few times — basically it's just adding an extra export. The description is: export the time of the user spent in the app. Alex Chen: Okay, I just need to remember it. I'm going to write it on Discord so I don't forget. Greg Palmer: Should we agree on one place for task management so that we know exactly where things are? Nina Torres: For me Notion works better — I've been keeping it up to date since the beginning of this four-week period.

Alex Chen: So basically we want to know the time that a user spent on Cibil in one session or in total. Nina Torres: In one session — then if we know sessions we'll also know intervals. Greg Palmer: So how many sessions they had and what's the average time spent? Nina Torres: We already know how many sessions — that's already in analytics. We just miss the duration. Alex Chen: What we could do is per session — see the first message and the last. Greg Palmer: There's already session count. It's only about adding how long the sessions were.

Alex Chen: So basically calculating it based on the data we already have. Greg Palmer: Yeah. I will walk you through — let's fix your permissions and then I'll show you what's there. Alex Chen: Nice. Okay, me and Greg we can stay. Nina Torres: I'm going to read the Kyra document that Morgan sent — I'm curious why the conclusion says it's better. That means all the work we're basing things off is gone, so we need to do a lot more than what we accounted for.
